adapted.adapter: The protocol 1 to 3 adapter turns an inspection's list of tools into a catalog without routers.
The protocol 1 to 3 adapter turns an inspection's list of tool summaries into a catalog summary without routers.
Every adapter for protocols 1 to 12 reads a bundle's requirements as user requirements: its accounts become accounts.user, and accounts.app is empty.

Every adapter for protocols 1 to 12 sends a bundle its invocation's user accounts as the flat record it reads, in the invocation (whose accounts protocols 1 to 5 carry only there) and in workflow step contexts. Such a bundle declares no app requirements, so it has no app accounts. Their accounts also carry a jwt_bearer provider as the secrets method it behaves as, like protocol 13's.

The protocol 13 adapter sends an account whose provider signs in with a service account key (the oauth2 method with grant jwt_bearer) as the secrets method it behaves as: the same fields, exposure and placements, labelled Service account. Its bundles never declare that method, so the invocation and workflow step contexts carry no member they reject.

additions.gate: The protocol 1 to 3 adapter drops kind before sending a call and refuses a call whose kind disagrees with the tool's queries. or mutations. prefix.
Sent only for a slot whose requirements declare health, which a protocol 1 to 4 build never does.
Sent only to a build whose requirements declare sql, which a protocol 1 to 9 build never does; their adapter refuses it.
Sent only to a build whose requirements declare capabilities.sharedDefinitions, which no protocol 1 to 12 build declares, nor a protocol 13 build from a release before the capability.
